ai.description: The Vellore Bridal Snake reaches 40–50 cm. It features a dark brown body with thin, white crossbars and a distinct white collar. A prominent white V-shaped mark distinguishes its head.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Lycodon nympha* is best identified by the distinct, broad white collar on its neck and the series of narrow, white, Y-shaped crossbands along its dark brown body.
ai.habitat: The Vellore Bridal Snake inhabits dry deciduous forests and scrublands in peninsular India, typically found at elevations ranging from sea level to 800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Vellore Bridal Snake is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to actively hunt for small geckos and skinks among rocky crevices and vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Vellore Bridal Snake is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Vellore Bridal Snake (*Lycodon nympha*) is found in peninsular India, primarily across the Western Ghats and parts of Tamil Nadu, at low to moderate elevations.
